editorial.thesis: A workshop-and-leisure city of about 7.0 million. Its retail is heavy on desserts, sweets & ice cream and fitness & wellness, and thin on grocery & daily needs and apparel, footwear & jewellery — and 0% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 86% of Delhi's. 16.14 chain outlets per lakh residents against 18.83 in Delhi; 40 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Apollo Pharmacy 186, Café Coffee Day 88, Domino's 80.

The mapped economy leans to desserts & sweets. Shares of all mapped places: desserts & sweets 1.2% (Delhi 0.7%); services & crafts 8.3% (Delhi 6.3%); grocery & daily needs 1.1% (Delhi 2.2%); automotive 2.2% (Delhi 3.0%). Raw counts would mislead because Delhi is mapped more completely (87,703 places against 66,688), so we compare mix, not counts.
No large under-served zone. No zone combines a large resident base with retail depth below 60% of the city average; the thin spots are small and scattered.

Retail is less concentrated than in Delhi. 46% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Delhi 47%). The largest cores are Strand Road · Brabourne Road (1,537 places) and Bidhannagar · Ring Road (1,488).

The widest brand gaps against Delhi. McDonald's 6 outlets vs 75; Domino's 80 outlets vs 140; Café Coffee Day 88 outlets vs 145. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 10 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Delhi, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Bidhannagar · Ring Road and Cit Road · Canal Circular Road are the largest zones by residents (173,000 and 139,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 46% of all commercial places, and Strand Road · Brabourne Road alone lists 1,537.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Sarat Bose Road · Lake Market holds 52 of the 1135 tracked chain outlets, and Cit Road · Canal Circular Road adds 51.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Bidhannagar · Ring Road and Gariahat Road · Hazra Road lead on education places (213 and 163, with 97 and 59 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. There is no large amber area. The blue cores include Strand Road · Brabourne Road.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (87,703 places in Delhi against 66,688 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Delhi; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Delhi, Kolkata's mapped places over-index on desserts & sweets (1.2% vs 0.7%), services & crafts (8.3% vs 6.3%), leisure & entertainment (4.1% vs 3.3%) and under-index on grocery & daily needs (1.1% vs 2.2%), automotive (2.2% vs 3.0%), malls & department stores (0.6% vs 0.8%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 1135 outlets of 40 tracked national brands within 10 km — 16.14 per lakh residents against Delhi's 18.83 (1289 outlets of 45 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Delhi are McDonald's (6 vs 75); Domino's (80 vs 140); Café Coffee Day (88 vs 145). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Delhi's, so low means thin by Delhi's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 10 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Kolkata's age mix against Delhi: children (0–14) 18.6% vs 23.1%, 15–24 18.4% vs 20.4%, working age 52.7% vs 49.7%, 60+ 10.3% vs 6.8%. Under-25s are 37% of residents.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 6.0% of mapped places against 5.7% in Delhi, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 80 (Delhi 140), Wow! Momo 79 (Delhi 32), KFC 38 (Delhi 51), Pizza Hut 36 (Delhi 68).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 2.7% of mapped places against 2.1% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 88 (Delhi 145), Blue Tokai 15 (Delhi 26), Starbucks 9 (Delhi 33), Chai Sutta Bar 3 (Delhi 0).
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 1.2% of mapped places against 0.7% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 53 (Delhi 29), Naturals 3 (Delhi 7). No mapped outlet in either city: Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 1.1% of mapped places against 2.2% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Spencer's 32 (Delhi 9), Big Bazaar 17 (Delhi 8), Reliance Smart / Fresh 15 (Delhi 21), DMart 14 (Delhi 7). No mapped outlet in either city: Star Bazaar.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.4% of mapped places against 1.2% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 186 (Delhi 108), MedPlus 78 (Delhi 0), Frank Ross 11 (Delhi 0). No mapped outlet in either city: Wellness Forever.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 5.2% of mapped places against 7.0% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 71 (Delhi 66), Raymond 38 (Delhi 55), Titan 38 (Delhi 21), Reliance Trends 33 (Delhi 22).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 8.3% of mapped places against 7.9% in Delhi, so the mix is level.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 3.2% of mapped places against 2.7% in Delhi — above its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 5.0% of mapped places against 3.9% in Delhi — above its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
